title: "Part 3 – Reproduction and exploration"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/cohabitation-one-day.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 3 is the centre of the day. Its first hour is Task 3: you reproduce a recorded result, find out what it rests on, and refit the published coefficient of the original authors (OAs) from the survey itself. The rest of the part opens the menu of alternatives and ends with a first exploration of it.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, Part 3 | The instruction of Task 2 of Multi100 read word for word, what it left open, and the aim of the reproduction: the test that analyst 5X3KG ran on the file that Multi100 gave the analysts. | 8 minutes |
| Task 3 in your report or working script, or [Browser lab](../../cases/cohabitation/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction) Task 3 | `check_score_file()` confirms that `data/score_person_months.csv` is the file that the analysts received. The chunk of Task 3 is the code of the analyst: the share of person-month rows that record a marriage in the 1995 survey against the share in the survey of 2006–2010, compared with `prop.test()`. It should give $\chi^2(1)$ = 47.474 on 23,949 rows, the value that Multi100 recorded for 5X3KG. Everyone types their value without sending it and sends it when the facilitator says go, so that the identical values appear at the same moment. In the browser lab the code of a marriage is left blank for you to fill in. | 12 minutes |
| Task 3, continued, and slides | The shares behind the test, which say that marriage became more common: the opposite of the claim. Then count the unions of the file, one row per woman, and set the 1995 cohort beside the 929 unions of the paper; the class sends its count of 1995 unions and marriages on "go". Then the file set beside the course rebuild survey by survey, how the 1995 rows of the file were built, the five analyses refitted on a file whose 1995 rows are repaired, and what a reproduction does and does not establish. Read the [codebook of the file](../../cases/cohabitation/data/score_person_months_codebook.md) if you finish early. | 18 minutes |
| Task 3, second part, and slides | `fit_spec(unions, adjust = "race_period")` refits Model 2 of the paper on the rebuilt unions: −0.686 (SE 0.138) against the published −0.683 (0.14). Then what that coefficient means beside an interaction of race-ethnicity and period, the change for non-Hispanic white women, and why the reference specification of the course, −0.730, leaves the interaction out. | 8 minutes |
| [Specification menu](../../cases/cohabitation/menu.qmd) and slides | The fifteen decisions at three levels, the six on which the curve keeps more than one option, the 144 specifications that they make, and the ground rules for the menu: change one decision at a time, and read the reason when an option is refused. | 10 minutes |
| Slides, the methods | Weights and the survey design, and why the total length of a union, which the file of the analysts carries, is a weaker control. An optional run of five slides covers [person-period data and the discrete-time model](../../companion/event-history.qmd): person-months, the monthly chance of marrying, the logit, the complementary log-log and the multinomial logit, the time since the start, and effect sizes on one scale. | 12 minutes |
| Task 4 in the workspace or on the [Browser lab](../../cases/cohabitation/lab.qmd#task-4-menu), then [Multiverse](../../cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd) | Call `try_spec()` with no arguments for the reference specification, then three or four times more, changing one argument at a time, and print the tries side by side with `my_experiments()`. Ask once for an option off the curve, such as `histories = "score_file"`, to read why it is refused. Then rerun the one that you would defend and send it with `submit_exploration()`. Your mark is drawn on the class chart as an open circle. | 22 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have reproduced $\chi^2$ = 47.474 yourself and found out what the file behind it holds for 1995; you have refitted the published coefficient from the survey and can say whose change it measures; you have tried three or four alternatives one argument at a time; and you have put an exploratory mark on the class chart.
